sources.title: CAG Report 10/2023: National Social Assistance Programme
sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
sources.summary: National pension audit separates diversion of administrative publicity funds from short-payment of entitled pensions; December 2022 Ministry replies retained.
limitations: Audit fieldwork covered 179 districts, 358 blocks, 699 Gram Panchayats and 8,461 surveyed beneficiaries; selected-district findings are not whole-population estimates.
Audit period precedes the recent five-year window; the report and response are recent evidence about historical delivery.
Direct original PDF returned HTTP 503; indexed original-document text archived. Original-site availability is not asserted.

sources.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

sources.summary: Final report examines beneficiary verification and take-home-ration supply during 2018-21, including the December 2022 government rebuttal.
limitations: The final audit replaces reliance on a 2022 draft reported in the prior NGO corpus.

sources.title: Lok Sabha AU695: loans sanctioned and disbursed under PM-SVANidhi

records.title: NSAP publicity funds used for other Ministry schemes
records.summary: CAG found ₹2.83 crore of NSAP IEC funds used for Ministry campaigns whose work orders named PMAY-G and DDU-GKY, with payment to DAVP before confirmation of execution. This is an audit finding about purpose and verification of expenditure, not a finding of partisan advertising or personal enrichment.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.period: 2017 work orders and expenditure; Ministry reply December 2022
records.response: The Ministry said in December 2022 that it had taken the matter up with its IEC division. A final recovery or reconciliation is not established in this record.
alternativeExplanations: Cross-scheme publicity can serve legitimate public-information aims, but that does not answer the audit’s earmarking and work-confirmation findings.
records.falsifier: Produce the approved expenditure-head correction, delivered-media receipts and final audit action-taken record.

amounts.stage: audited expenditure from NSAP IEC funds for other-scheme publicity

records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Chhattisgarh: pensions did not start from the effective date
records.summary: In selected Chhattisgarh districts, Table 6.2 records 61,913 pension cases and ₹3,917 lakh of short-payment because disbursal did not begin from the sanctioned effective date. These are people missing entitled support, not beneficiaries alleged to have committed fraud.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Selected districts within Chhattisgarh; this table does not name them, so no district coverage is invented.

records.period: Audit FY2017-18 to FY2020-21; reply December 2022
records.response: The Ministry said in December 2022 that observations had been referred to the concerned states/UTs. The table does not show subsequent settlement of these arrears.
alternativeExplanations: Processing and bank failures may explain delay; later catch-up payment could change outstanding liability.
records.falsifier: Reconcile sanction effective dates with dated bank-credit and arrears-payment records for the 61,913 cases.
limitations: Not a complete count of all Chhattisgarh pensioners; do not add to overlapping national short-payment totals.
records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Madhya Pradesh: reconcile ration orders with beneficiary counts
records.summary: The final CAG report contrasts supply orders for 5.51 lakh out-of-school adolescent-girl entries with Rajya Shiksha Kendra’s 0.43 lakh estimate for 2018-21. THR supply value was ₹122.99 crore: ₹100.90 crore paid and ₹22.09 crore pending. CAG estimated ₹110.78 crore of likely avoidable excess; that estimate is neither an additional payment nor a proved recovery.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.period: FY2018-19 to FY2020-21; unpaid bills position 31 March 2022; government reply December 2022
records.response: Government said its numbers were correct on projected 2001 Census figures, that a baseline survey had occurred and supply orders used MIS data; it promised action where lapses occurred. CAG rejected the explanation because no reliable survey evidence was supplied and the methods were inconsistent.
alternativeExplanations: Census estimates, annual beneficiary entries and distinct persons are different populations; only matched-age, matched-period beneficiary verification can settle them.
Record defects may explain some discrepancies; criminal intent cannot be assigned to all recipients or workers.
records.falsifier: Produce the contemporaneous baseline survey, age/education eligibility, unique beneficiary reconciliation, receipt registers and paid-bill ledger.

amounts.stage: recorded THR supply value including paid and pending bills
paid component of ₹122.99 crore supply value
pending unpaid component of ₹122.99 crore supply value
CAG estimated likely avoidable excess, not an additional payment

limitations: The four money figures overlap and must never be summed.
No current recovery amount established.
records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Odisha: nutrition coverage fell below recorded enrolment
records.summary: Across six test-checked DSWOs, CAG tabulated 57,64,642 cumulative enrolment entries and 55,66,539 service-coverage entries in 2018-23, a gap of 1,98,103. Thirteen of 121 surveyed beneficiaries reported exclusion connected with Poshan enrolment, Aadhaar linkage, temporary migration or other reasons.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.response: Government said in June 2025 that efforts were being made for 100% Aadhaar enrolment and coverage. The record does not establish that the sampled gap had subsequently closed.
alternativeExplanations: Repeated annual enrolment means the cumulative gap need not equal distinct individuals.
Migration and enrolment reconciliation can affect denominators; exclusion reasons from 13 interviews do not explain every gap entry.
records.falsifier: Reconcile age-eligible, deduplicated monthly enrolment with service registers and transfer/migration records for the six sampled districts.
limitations: Table 2.5: Balangir 73,639; Ganjam 77,995; Jharsuguda 34,242; Mayurbhanj 8,671; Puri 0; Rayagada 3,556 missing-coverage entries.
The table’s zero for Puri does not establish universal service quality there.
records.dateBasis: Exact publication day unresolved; audit and response periods are stated separately.

records.title: Odisha: verify substitute food during hot-meal interruptions
records.summary: In 45 of 60 sampled Anganwadi centres, CAG recorded 62,100 hot-cooked-meal days against 65,400 required, a deficit of 3,300 centre-days during 2018-23. This unit is centre-days, not 3,300 individual children or a statewide count.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: 60 sampled AWCs in six selected DSWOs; the extracted aggregate does not allocate the 45 affected AWCs by district.

records.response: Government attributed interruptions to COVID-19 and extreme summer heat, saying dry rations replaced cooked meals. CAG could not verify that response because the sampled AWCs lacked distribution records for the interruption period.
alternativeExplanations: Documented delivery of nutritionally appropriate dry rations could explain service substitution without denial of food.
Missing records alone do not establish that no dry ration was delivered.
records.falsifier: Produce dated closure orders, beneficiary acknowledgements and quantity/nutrition records for replacement rations covering the 3,300 centre-days.
limitations: This is a service-continuity and verification question, not a diagnosis of malnutrition caused by the programme.
records.dateBasis: Exact publication day unresolved; audit and response periods are stated separately.

records.title: Tamil Nadu: housing names replaced without household matching
records.summary: CAG identified 981 UNKNOWN-name replacements in eight sampled blocks and tested 595 of 5,949 similar cases in non-sampled blocks, finding 566 ineligible replacements. It estimated ₹27.52 crore loss associated with 1,547 suspected fraudulent sanctions. The untested similar cases are not counted as proven ineligible.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.period: PMAY-G audit 2016-17 to 2020-21; government reply March 2022
records.response: Government said the District Rural Development Agencies would verify eligibility and initiate action against officials responsible for falsification. The retained finding does not establish a completed recovery.
alternativeExplanations: Legitimate replacement can occur for a real household member; the audit’s issue is cross-household substitution, tested with records and physical checks.
No inference of fraud is made solely from a name correction or surname similarity.
records.falsifier: Reconcile the original SECC household, authorised replacement, MGNREGS household linkage, sanction and bank recipient for each identified case.

amounts.stage: CAG estimated loss associated with 1,547 suspect sanctions; not certified total cash recovered

limitations: 1,547 equals 981 plus 566 verified non-sampled-block cases; it is not 981 plus all 5,949 similar records.
No private beneficiary identifiers reproduced.
records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: PM-SVANidhi: distinguish vendors, loans and fiscal cost
records.summary: At 12 July 2026, Parliament reports 1.15 crore loans worth ₹18,475.06 crore disbursed to 76.95 lakh vendors. Successive tranches explain why loans exceed people. The reply provides separate state-year sanctions, disbursements and amounts, but no numeric repayment-rate answer.
records.status: Government-reported programme accounting; no irregularity inferred

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.period: Cumulative inception to 12 July 2026; Annexure I FY2021-22 to FY2025-26
records.response: MoHUA describes staged loan repayment, periodic reviews and graded expansion beyond statutory urban areas. It cites an ISB study reporting around 20% borrower income growth in 2023-25; the independent study was not opened here.
alternativeExplanations: Repeat tranches are an intended feature, not duplicate-beneficiary fraud.
Changing credit demand, lender decisions and repayment status affect annual disbursement; a fall in counts does not itself prove exclusion.
records.falsifier: Obtain distinct borrower/tranche keys, sanction and bank-credit dates, repayment cohorts and government subsidy/guarantee accounts before measuring defaults or net public cost.

amounts.stage: cumulative loan principal disbursed; not government grant expenditure

records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Keonjhar constituency: named NGO special-school grants
records.summary: Parliament names Voluntary Organisation for Rural Improvement as DDRS-supported operator of a school for hearing and visual disability in Keonjhar Lok Sabha constituency: ₹53,00,235 released with 65 beneficiaries in FY2023-24 and ₹18,28,446 with 62 in FY2024-25. FY2025-26 is a dash for amount and beneficiaries.
records.status: Named grant release confirmed in Parliament; utilisation and current operation unverified

geography.note: Constituency association only. No equivalence to Keonjhar district boundaries or a particular school campus is assumed.

records.response: The Ministry confirms the named service and releases. The answer does not provide a reason for the FY2025-26 dash or a utilisation certificate.
alternativeExplanations: Grant timing, unspent balance, application status or changing eligibility could affect annual release; none is established for this recipient.
A dash does not establish school closure or denial of all services.
records.falsifier: Check institution registration, sanction orders, utilisation certificates, attendance and the next release decision before assessing continuity.
records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Dahod: district disability-service releases need utilisation context
records.summary: The original answer records DDRS releases of ₹46,20,561 in FY2023-24 and ₹17,52,181 in FY2024-25 for Dahod district, with a dash in FY2025-26. These are a district funding series, not grants to every NGO or proof of reduced service coverage.
records.status: District release series documented; recipient allocation and utilisation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.response: The answer supplies releases and describes a January 2026 Purple Fair in Dahod through CRC Ahmedabad, but does not explain the DDRS release change or identify the district recipients.
alternativeExplanations: A grant-release reduction can reflect balances, application timing or scheme transitions; none of these is verified for Dahod.
records.falsifier: Obtain recipient-wise sanction and utilisation records plus service attendance before connecting release changes to outcomes.

amounts.stage: central DDRS grant released to district programmes
central DDRS grant released to district programmes

records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Uttar Pradesh: no fresh PMMVY release does not mean no funding
records.summary: The PMMVY annexure shows NIL central release in FY2024-25 and 0 in FY2025-26 for Uttar Pradesh. Its explicit footnote says funds were not released because adequate funds were available in the SNA account. This is a control against treating a zero release as proof that maternity benefits stopped.
records.status: Government accounting explanation documented; beneficiary outcomes not inferred

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.response: MWCD attributes non-release to adequate SNA balances and describes SNA/SNA-SPARSH funding rules. The answer does not establish bank-credit success for every eligible mother.
alternativeExplanations: Existing balances can fund current spending despite no fresh central transfer.
Cash held in an SNA account also does not prove timely delivery to beneficiaries.
records.falsifier: Reconcile opening SNA balance, releases, state share, expenditure and beneficiary-bank credits for the same period.

amounts.stage: fresh central release reported NIL; not total funds available

records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Kerala: scholarship payments initiated but returned to treasury
records.summary: CAG found 2,360 pre-matric state-scholarship transactions worth ₹30.24 lakh rejected and returned to government during 2019-22, and 7,438 post-matric transactions worth ₹43.14 lakh during 2018-21. Institutions could see Payment Initiated without confirming bank credit. These are rejected transactions, not proven theft or unique-student counts.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Geography limited to the named programme/audit area, not inferred from the publisher address.

records.period: Pre-matric FY2019-20 to FY2021-22; post-matric FY2018-19 to FY2020-21; data snapshot June 2022
records.response: Government said in June 2023 that monitoring lakhs of payments was impractical and e-grantz had added auto-generated rejection/profile-verification alerts. CAG said the reply did not resolve payment to already-rejected claimants and institutions needed credit-status visibility.
alternativeExplanations: Invalid accounts, IFSC details or frozen accounts can cause rejection without deliberate exclusion.
Subsequent corrections after the June 2022 data snapshot could resolve particular cases; no current unpaid total is asserted.
records.falsifier: Join approved claims to bank response files, treasury returns and successful re-presentment dates, deduplicated by student and instalment.

amounts.stage: rejected pre-matric transactions returned to government
rejected post-matric transactions returned to government

limitations: Amounts concern different schemes and partly overlapping years; no cross-scheme unique-beneficiary total is derived.
records.dateBasis: Publication/Parliament-answer observation date, not the underlying transaction date.

records.title: Jharkhand: doubtful scholarship entries need identity reconciliation
records.summary: CAG identified ₹40.31 lakh granted through 410 applications associated with 205 student records sharing name, father’s name and bank account but using different UID values. It calls the grant doubtful because Aadhaar validation controls were absent; this does not adjudicate identity fraud by each student.
records.status: Historical audit finding; current remediation unverified

geography.note: Jharkhand-administered scholarship scheme includes 201 within-state and four outside-state students; outside institution locations are not identified here.

records.period: Application analysis FY2017-18 to FY2019-20; overall audit April 2017 to July 2020; referral October 2022
records.response: The chapter says the matter was referred to the State Government in October 2022 and its reply was awaited. No final recovery, adjudication or later departmental response is established in this evidence slice.
alternativeExplanations: Data-entry error, correction, migration between courses or identity mismatch require individual reconciliation; repeated applications alone do not prove criminal intent.
records.falsifier: Obtain authenticated identity-correction history, course eligibility, application approvals, bank-credit confirmation and the audit action-taken reply.

amounts.stage: scholarships granted that CAG classified as doubtful; not confirmed recovered loss

limitations: The ₹38.31 lakh within-state and ₹2 lakh outside-state components are included in ₹40.31 lakh, not added again.
No student names or private identifiers are exposed.
records.dateBasis: Official report tabling date, not the underlying application or payment date.
